title: How the Buck and Bubbles spot fit into Nazarro's acrobatic act
summary: Nazarro's acrobatic act ended with a missed trick and a gag that brought on Buck and Bubbles; Bubbles says they never worked blackface after Louisville.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: You weren't going black-faced any more?
You said you performed along with Nat Nazarro's act.
How did the two acts combine?
only thing he did was acrobatics. He was an understander, he had a top mounter. He thought a one-man trick and missed the trick, that's when he introduced us.

Yeah, acrobatics. He's an underlander. He juggled a kid around he'd do a flag up, he'd do a -- the kid would do a back somersalt, back flips and they'd do handstands. It was an acrobatic act. You know what acrobats are?
And how would Buck and Bubbles play into that?

No, we didn't play into that. The idea was he'd do that part and then he'd miss the trick, the one-hand trick, which is his last trick. He missed the last trick, understand? With the one hand? And when he missed the trick he'd pull a gag to him by his boy -- "every time I stay out late you come home drunk. One of these days

you'll be out drinking and I'll come home drunk." This gag. He missed this trick. "Ladies and gentlemen, I had to be at Carnegie Hall the other night, two gentlemen asked me if I'd insist them running their recital in vaudeville so I thought I'd run them along. Are the gentlemen there? I think one of them plays a flute in four feet deep of rice pudding. Buck and Bubbles? Bring them on." Here we come. I told you how we're dressed. Okay. On. That's how we got on the act. Now we do our song and dance and we burned it.
